questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: in which where i could expect big cultural differences, and therefore not only learn from the university but also the country in itself

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: pretty easy, but without specific help from the university it would have been immensely harder.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: we had a contact person who helped us with any ordeals we had to arrange - living quaters, valuta exchange and means of transport (car)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: easy, in the way that we had a contact person who helped us greatly

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: that a car is an absolute must-have

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: to be honest, i dont really remember the registration process - it was as if we arrived, and then we were enrolled in the class. i remember having a big meeting with the officials of the school and the head of our institute in which they explanied what the courses would include. But the promises were not realistic.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: i guess we could ask whoever for help, but most knew nothing about the technicalities of Erasmus

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: there was only 1 class

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
to not get your hopes up about everything they're saying they're offering. All of the excursions they mentioned never happened.
This was never a problem for me and my classmates because we arranged most of our trips ourselves, and still had a great time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i had what is called Regular Arabic Intensive Intermediate 1, 2 and 3 in the semester spring 2025.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: very different. We were seated as in public school and had one main teacher for the whole course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Regular Arabic Intensive Intermediate 1, 2 and 3.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the same, as they have no other means for students of middle eastern studies i think.

questions.answer: I had a wisdom teeth removal, but it only costs 300 DKK. so i was fine. I guess i didn't expect to use the car as much as we did (we were 4 people sharing 1 car), but gas was cheap.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the food was a lot less expensive than i've had originally imagined.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: they had a day where students could show off their culture in a big hall. But other than that, the available clubs didn't really appeal to non-omani students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: for sure, they should visit nearby cities and historical cites. Also the amazing nature Oman has to offer.  This includes : Jabal Shams, Jabal Al-Akhdar, Misfah al-abriyeen. And all the wadi's expecially - wadi shab, wadi hawer, wadi bani khalid and others.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy once you've realised what is appropiate and what is not. The clothes, the way of talking.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: What to wear. What not to wear. I almost didn't use any of the clothes that i had brought with me to the country. Bought most of it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the welcoming people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. be sure that you know what you need signed for erasmus, and ask for at copy.
2. if some of the other students are behaving strangely, as in fx taking pictures of you without your permission - don't be afraid to tell them no. Their fascination will pass, and a lot of them are just wants to be friends. 
3. expect different ways of learning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: i don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: that slowly, but steady, the confidence in arabic speech had improved greatly.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: i don't know... The exams i guess?

questions.answer: Yes
